tier_note: in-training loss monitor over 160 FIXED held-out windows; a WM/readout diagnostic. NEVER driving performance, and NOT the four binding metric families.

estimator_refusal.reason: each eval_* value is ALREADY the pooled mean over the 160 windows; metrics.jsonl carries no per-window values and no episode index, and taniteval.ci.episode_cluster_bootstrap requires both. No estimator can produce an interval from this file.
estimator_refusal.consequence: every era-level statement derived here is a DIRECTION, not a verdict.

fixed_window_set_invariants.meaning: constant => the same 160 windows at every step and across every relaunch, so the eval series is step-to-step comparable. If any value varies, EVERY cross-step eval comparison in this output is withdrawn.

A_pre_nav_leaked.note: |delta| / sd_step is a DESCRIPTIVE signal-to-scatter ratio, NOT a t-statistic and NOT a CI: the points are autocorrelated and share one 160-window sample.

C_clean.note: |delta| / sd_step is a DESCRIPTIVE signal-to-scatter ratio, NOT a t-statistic and NOT a CI: the points are autocorrelated and share one 160-window sample.

train_eval_gap.caveat: train rows are 20-window samples of the CURRENT batches; the eval is a fixed 160-window set. The two are DIFFERENT windows, so only the TREND of the gap is interpretable, never its absolute level.

pace.note: Two DIFFERENT clocks, not the same probe twice. probe B includes relaunch startup, so it reads slightly slower than probe A by construction.

projection.evidence: ESTIMATED (assumes no further death and a stable rate)
